summary: Coto de Caza is one of the largest gated communities in the United States, sprawling across roughly 7.8 square miles of the Santa Ana Mountains foothills in southern Orange County — a detail that surprises people who picture gated living as a compact enclave rather than an entire census-designated place with its own zip code, equestrian trails, and canyon-carved terrain rolling eastward toward Cleveland National Forest. The landscape delivers golden-hour views over ridgelines thick with coastal sage scrub, and residents have direct trail access into Caspers Wilderness Park and Thomas F. Riley Wilderness Park at the community's edges, making evening hikes a geographic convenience rather than a weekend excursion. But this is emphatically a bedroom community: there is virtually no commercial job center within the gates, so employment — largely in the Irvine–Lake Forest–Mission Viejo tech, medical-device, and financial-services corridors — means a car commute along Oso Parkway to the 241 toll road or the congested I-5. The median home value of roughly $1.42 million against a median household income near $232,000 produces a price-to-income ratio just above 6:1, tight but more plausible than much of coastal Orange County, while median rent above $3,500 reflects the near-total absence of multifamily housing stock. With 280-plus sunny days a year and average highs around 73°F, the climate is almost monotonously pleasant — the defining tradeoff is that you're trading walkable retail, restaurants, and urban texture for space, silence, and uninterrupted hillside sky.
